explanation: A king from Salem who was also a priest of the Most High, a figure with no recorded genealogy or birth date that serves as a picture of Christ.
An ancient name for the city of Jerusalem, meaning "peace," representing the place where Melchizedek ruled.
The function of representing people before God through sacrifices and prayers; the chapter contrasts the Levitical priesthood with Christ's eternal service.
One of Israel's twelve tribes chosen to perform religious duties in the temple under the Law of Moses.
The portion (one-tenth) of income or harvest that Abraham gave to Melchizedek, symbolizing recognition and honor for a higher authority.
A description of Christ's priesthood which has no end, unlike earthly priests who died; he lives forever to intercede before God.
A holy agreement between God and humanity, where the chapter emphasizes that Jesus is the guarantor of a new and better covenant than the old law provided.
